Nova Launcher uses Nova Actions to perform some system functions, like expanding the notification shade or showing the recent apps screen.

On some devices or Android versions, Accessibility access is required for certain Nova Actions to work. If Accessibility access is required on your device, you'll be prompted to enable it. Otherwise, there's no need to grant access.

Nova doesn't watch any user action by way of this Accessibility access, though the privilege to do so is required for all accessibility services. Nova disregards any event sent by the system.

In order to expand notifications or show the recent app menu with a gesture, swipe, or icon tap, Nova uses the performGlobalAction Accessibility service.

This Nova Actions requires Accessibility permission. Nova only uses Accessibility\'s performGlobalAction method in order to perform some Nova Actions. However this is a sensitive permission that also allows monitoring other apps. Nova Launcher is not configured for that functionality and receives no events.
